speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility; please tell me your age and specific height and weight measurements to begin our assessment.

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The combination of ambiguous genitalia (partial labial fusion, clitoromegaly) at birth, severe acne, and bone fragility suggests a complex endocrine disorder. To confirm, have you or your mother noticed excessive hair growth (hirsutism) elsewhere on the body, and have any blood tests been done to check your androgen and 17-hydroxyprogesterone levels?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of ambiguous genitalia at birth, delayed menarche, severe acne, and bone fragility strongly suggests Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH), likely due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. To confirm this, I need to see your recent hormone panel.

REQUEST TEST: Serum_17-Hydroxyprogesterone, Serum_Testosterone, Serum_Estradiol, and 17-Hydroxyprogesterone to Cortisol ratio.
REQUEST TEST: Bone_Density_Scan.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency)
